mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals tighter monetary policy, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 4%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises for four months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 70% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, coupled with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals labor market stress that reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS drops >1% MoM AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the monetary aggregate RSAFS (Reserves) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5%, while FEDFUNDS remains stable, signals liquidity tightening that increases funding costs and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA by >5% AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
regime_hint: neutral monetary policy with liquidity shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such liquidity-tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds its 12-month MA by >10% for three months, but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation surge (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%) coincident with stagnant industrial production (INDPRO flat or declining for two months) signals cost-push inflation, which erodes real corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% AND INDPRO flat or down for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such inflation/weak-growth episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 3.5% for four months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes.
